verses.text: These are the words of the Preacher, David's son, king in Jerusalem.
“It's a breath, just a breath,” says the Preacher. “It all slips away like a breath.”
What do people actually get to keep from all the work they do under the sun?
One generation goes and another comes along, but the earth stays put forever.
The sun comes up, goes down, then hurries back to where it rises again.
The wind heads south, swings north, and keeps circling back around to the same routes.
Every river runs into the sea, but the sea never fills up. The rivers flow back to the places they always flow.
Everything is more exhausting than words can say. Your eyes never see enough, and your ears never hear enough.
What's happened will happen again. What's been done will be done again. There's nothing new under the sun.
Can you point to something and say, “Look, this is new”? It was here ages before we were.
Nobody remembers the people who came before. And people still to come will be forgotten by the ones who come after them too.
I, the Preacher, was king over Israel in Jerusalem.
I put my whole heart into using wisdom to figure out everything people do under the sky. What a heavy load God has given people to struggle with.
I've seen everything people do under the sun. Look at it all. It's a breath that slips away, like trying to catch the wind.
You can't straighten what's bent, and you can't count what's missing.
I told myself, “Look, I've gained more wisdom than anyone who came before me in Jerusalem. I've gotten to know wisdom and knowledge firsthand.”
I put my whole heart into understanding wisdom, madness, and foolishness. I realized this was another way of chasing the wind.
A lot of wisdom brings a lot of grief. The more you know, the more you hurt.
I told myself, “Come on, let's try having a good time. Go enjoy yourself.” And look, that slipped away like a breath too.
I looked at laughter and said, “That's foolish.” I looked at having fun and asked, “What does it actually do?”
I thought about lifting my mood with wine while still letting wisdom guide me. I tried foolishness too, to see what was worth doing under heaven in the handful of days people have to live.
I took on huge projects. I built houses for myself and planted vineyards.
I laid out gardens and parks and planted all kinds of fruit trees in them.
I built pools to water the grove where the trees were growing.
I bought men and women as servants, and others were born into my household. I had more herds and flocks than anyone who'd come before me in Jerusalem.
I piled up silver and gold and treasures from kings and provinces. I brought in men and women to sing for me, plus all sorts of instruments people love to hear.
I became great and gained more than anyone before me in Jerusalem. My wisdom stayed with me through all of it.
Whatever caught my eye, I let myself have it. I never held my heart back from a good time. The joy I took in all my hard work was the share I got from it.
Then I looked at everything my hands had made and all the work it took. Look at it. All of it slipped away like a breath, like chasing the wind. There was nothing to keep from it under the sun.
I turned to look at wisdom, madness, and foolishness. What can the next king do anyway? The same things that were done ages ago.
I saw that wisdom beats foolishness by as much as light beats darkness.
Wise people can see where they're going, and fools walk in the dark. But I saw them all meet the same fate.
I told myself, “What happens to a fool will happen to me too. So what did getting wiser do for me?” I realized this too slipped away like a breath.
Nobody remembers the wise forever any more than they remember fools. In the days ahead, both will be long forgotten. The wise die just like fools!
So I hated life. Everything done under the sun weighed on me. It all slips away like a breath, like chasing the wind.
I hated all the work I'd done under the sun because I'd have to leave it to whoever came after me.
Who knows if they'll be wise or foolish? Either way they'll be in charge of everything I worked for and put my wisdom into under the sun. This too slips away like a breath.
That's when I started to lose heart over all the work I'd done under the sun.
You can work with wisdom, knowledge, and skill, then have to hand everything over to someone who did none of the work. That's a breath slipping away and a terrible wrong.
What do people get from all their work and all the effort they pour into it under the sun?
Their days are full of pain, and their work wears them down. Even at night their minds won't rest. This too slips away like a breath.
There's nothing better for people than to eat, drink, and take some joy in their work. I saw that this too comes from God's hand.
Who could eat or enjoy life more than I could?

God gives wisdom, knowledge, and joy to the person who pleases him. He gives the sinner the work of gathering and piling things up to hand them over to someone who pleases God. This too slips away like a breath, like chasing the wind.
Everything has its season. There's a time for every purpose under heaven.
A time to be born and a time to die. A time to plant and a time to pull up what you planted.
A time to kill and a time to heal. A time to tear down and a time to build up.
A time to cry and a time to laugh. A time to grieve and a time to dance.
A time to throw stones away and a time to gather them up. A time to hold someone close and a time to keep your arms to yourself.
A time to look for something and a time to let it go as lost. A time to keep and a time to throw away.
A time to tear and a time to sew. A time to stay quiet and a time to speak up.
A time to love and a time to hate. A time for war and a time for peace.
What does a worker actually get from all that work?
I've seen the heavy work God has given people to struggle with.
He's made everything beautiful at the right time. He's put eternity in people's hearts, yet they can't see the whole of what God has done from beginning to end.
I know there's nothing better for people than to find joy and do good as long as they're alive.
When people can eat, drink, and enjoy something good from their work, that's a gift from God.
I know whatever God does lasts forever. You can't add anything to it or take anything away. God made it that way so people would stand in awe before him.
What's here now was here a long time ago. What's coming was here long ago too. God goes looking for what has passed away.
I saw something else under the sun. The very place where justice should be was full of wickedness, and I found wickedness where people were supposed to do right.
I told myself, “God will judge both the people who do right and the wicked. There's a time for every purpose and every deed.”
I told myself, “God tests people so they'll see that they're like animals.

What happens to people happens to animals too. They all meet the same fate. One dies and so does the other. They all breathe the same breath. People have no advantage over animals, because it all slips away like a breath.
They all go to the same place. Everything comes from dust, and everything goes back to dust.
Who knows whether a person's spirit goes up and an animal's spirit goes down into the earth?”
So I saw there's nothing better than for people to enjoy the work they do. That's their share. Who can bring them back to see what happens after they're gone?

I looked again at all the oppression happening under the sun. I saw the tears of the people being crushed, with nobody to comfort them. The people crushing them had all the power, and still there was nobody to comfort them.
So I counted those who'd been dead a long time better off than the people still alive.
Better off than either is the person who hasn't been born, who's never seen the evil people do under the sun.
Then I saw how all that hard work and achievement makes neighbors envy each other. That too slips away like a breath, like chasing the wind.
A fool folds their hands and lets their own life fall apart.
Better to have one handful and some peace than two handfuls that cost you endless work and leave you chasing the wind.
I looked again and saw something else slipping away under the sun.

Here's someone all alone, with no son or brother. Their work never ends, and they never see enough money to feel satisfied. “Who am I working for, then? Why am I cutting myself off from anything good?” That too slips away like a breath. What a miserable way to spend your life.
Two are better than one. They get a good return for the work they put in together.
If one falls, the other can help them up. But it's awful to fall when you're alone and nobody's there to lift you.
If two people lie down together, they can keep warm. How's one person supposed to stay warm alone?
Someone can overpower one person, but two can stand against them. A cord of three strands won't snap in a hurry.
A poor kid with wisdom is better than an old king who's too foolish to listen when someone corrects him.
That young man came out of prison to be king, even though he was born poor in that very kingdom.
I saw all the people walking under the sun side with the young man who took the older king's place.
There was no end to the crowd he ruled. But the people who come later won't celebrate him. That too slips away like a breath, like chasing the wind.
Watch your step when you go to God's house. It's better to come close and listen than to offer the sacrifice fools bring. They don't even know they're doing wrong.
Don't let words fly out of your mouth or rush to say whatever's on your heart before God. God's in heaven and you're on earth, so keep your words few.
Many worries will fill your sleep with dreams, and a fool fills the air with words.
When you make God a vow, don't put off keeping it. Fools don't please him. Do what you promised.
It's better to skip the vow than make one and fail to keep it.
Don't let your mouth talk you into sin. Don't tell the messenger, “I made a mistake.” Why make God angry at what you say and have him wreck what your hands built?
Piles of dreams can all slip away like a breath, and so can piles of words. Stand in awe of God.
If you see poor people oppressed and justice and fairness torn away in some district, don't be shocked. One official has a higher official watching them, and others sit above them too.
What the land produces is for everybody. Even the king gets his share from the fields.
Love money and you'll never have enough money. Love having more and you'll never be satisfied with what comes in. That too slips away like a breath.
The more goods there are, the more people show up to eat them. What does the owner get besides a chance to look at it all?
A worker sleeps sweetly after eating a little or a lot. Rich people have so much they can't sleep.
I've seen something awful under the sun. Someone holds on to their wealth, and it ends up hurting them.
Then a stroke of bad luck wipes the money out. If they've had a son, there's nothing left to put in his hand.
They came out of their mother's womb naked, and they'll leave the same way. They won't carry off a single thing they worked for.
That's another terrible wrong. People leave exactly as they came. What does anybody gain from working for the wind?
They spend their days eating in the dark, full of frustration, sickness, and anger.
Here's what I've seen is good and right. Eat, drink, and take some joy in the work you do under the sun in the days God gives you. That's your share.
When God gives someone riches and possessions and lets them enjoy those things, take their share, and find joy in their work, that's God's gift.
They won't spend much time dwelling on how many days they've got, because God keeps their heart busy with joy.
I've seen something wrong under the sun, and it weighs heavy on people.

God gives someone riches, possessions, and honor, so they've got everything their heart could want. Yet God doesn't let them enjoy any of it, and a stranger gets to eat it all. It slips away like a breath. It's a terrible sickness.
Say a man has a hundred kids and lives a very long time. If he never gets to enjoy anything good and doesn't even get a burial, I say a stillborn child is better off.
The child comes and goes like a breath, leaving in darkness, with even its name hidden in the dark.
It never saw the sun or knew it, but it has more rest than that man.
Even if someone lived a thousand years twice over without enjoying anything good, don't they all end up in the same place?
People work to put food in their mouths, and their appetite still won't say it's had enough.
So what advantage does a wise person have over a fool? What does a poor person gain from knowing how to get along in the world?
Better to have what's right in front of you than let your desires wander everywhere. This too slips away like a breath, like chasing the wind.
Whatever exists got its name long ago. What a human being is has already been made known. People can't go up against someone stronger than they are.
More words just give you more that slips away like a breath. What does anybody gain from that?
Who knows what's good for someone in this life, in all those fleeting days that pass like a shadow? Who can tell them what will happen under the sun after they're gone?
A good name beats fine perfume, and the day you die is better than the day you're born.
It's better to go to a house where people are grieving than to a house where they're partying. Death is where everybody's headed, and the living ought to take that to heart.
Sorrow can do more good than laughter. A sad face can go with a heart that's getting better.
Wise hearts are with people who mourn. Fools have their hearts set on the party.
You're better off hearing a wise person correct you than listening to fools sing.
A fool's laughter sounds like thorns crackling under a pot. This too slips away like a breath.
Extortion can turn a wise person into a fool, and a bribe wrecks their judgment.
The end of something is better than its beginning. A patient spirit is better than a proud one.
Don't let your temper flare up in a hurry. Anger makes itself right at home in fools.
Don't ask, “Why were the old days better than these?” There's no wisdom in asking it like that.
Wisdom is as good as getting an inheritance, and it's an advantage for anyone still living under the sun.
Wisdom can protect you just like money can. The edge knowledge gives you is that wisdom keeps its owner alive.
Take a good look at what God has done. Who can straighten out something he bent?
When things are going well, enjoy them. When things go badly, stop and think. God made both kinds of days, side by side, so no one can figure out what's coming after them.
In these fleeting days of mine I've seen it all. Someone who does right dies while still doing right, and somebody wicked lives on and on doing evil.
Don't go overboard trying to be righteous or make yourself out to be overly wise. Why wreck yourself?
Don't go deep into wickedness or act a fool. Why die before your time?
Hold on to this advice, and keep hold of the other part too. Someone who stands in awe of God can come through it all.
Wisdom gives a wise person more strength than ten rulers can give a city.
There isn't a person on earth who does good and never sins.
Don't listen in on everything people say. You might hear your servant cursing you.
Deep down you know there have been plenty of times when you cursed somebody too.
I tested all this with wisdom. I told myself, “I'm going to be wise.” But wisdom stayed out of reach.
What's real lies far away and goes incredibly deep. Who can get to the bottom of it?
I turned my heart to digging for answers, looking for wisdom and how everything fits together. I wanted to understand how wickedness is stupidity and foolishness is madness.
I found something more bitter than death: a woman whose heart is all snares and traps and whose hands are chains. Whoever pleases God gets away from her, but a sinner gets caught.
“Look what I found,” says the Preacher. “I put one thing next to another, trying to work out an explanation.
My soul is still looking for it, and I haven't found it. I found one man out of a thousand, but I didn't find one woman among them all.
Here's the only thing I've found. God made people upright, but they've gone off looking for all sorts of schemes.”
Who compares to someone wise? Who can tell you what a thing really means? Wisdom lights up a person's face and softens that hard look.
Here's what I say: follow the king's command, because of the oath you made to God.
Don't rush out of his presence or dig in your heels over something wrong. He'll do whatever he pleases.
The king's word carries the highest authority. Who can ask him, “What are you doing?”
Follow the command and you'll stay out of harm's way. A wise heart knows when to act and how to go about it.
There's a time and a way for every purpose, even when misery weighs heavy on a person.
Nobody knows what's going to happen. Who can tell them how it'll go?
Nobody has the power to hold their spirit in or decide the day they'll die. You don't get discharged in the middle of a war, and doing evil won't get evildoers out of trouble.
I saw all this and gave my attention to everything done under the sun. There are times when people use their power to hurt others.
I saw wicked people buried. They'd even come from the holy place, then they were gone and forgotten in the same city where they'd done those things. This too slips away like a breath.
When a sentence for doing wrong takes too long to be carried out, people make up their minds to do evil.
A sinner might do wrong a hundred times and still live a long life. Even so, I know things will go better for people who stand in awe of God and honor him.
Things won't go well for the wicked. Their days won't stretch out like a shadow, because they don't stand in awe of God.

Here's something on earth that slips away like a breath. People who do right get what the wicked deserve, and wicked people get what those who do right deserve. I said this too slips away like a breath.
So I spoke up for joy. There's nothing better under the sun than to eat, drink, and enjoy yourself. That joy can go with you in your work through all the days God gives you under the sun.
I put my whole heart into understanding wisdom and watching what goes on here on earth, even when people's eyes get no sleep day or night.

Then I saw what God does. People can't figure out the work that goes on under the sun. No matter how hard they try, they won't get to the bottom of it. Even someone wise who thinks they can work it out still won't be able to.

I took all this to heart and looked into it. People who do right, people who are wise, and everything they do are in God's hands. Nobody knows whether love or hate is waiting for them. It all lies ahead.

The same fate comes to everyone, the righteous and the wicked, the good, the clean and the unclean, the person who offers a sacrifice and the one who doesn't. It comes to the good and the sinner, the one who takes an oath and the one who's afraid to take one.
Here's what's wrong with everything under the sun. The same fate comes for everybody. People have hearts full of evil and madness while they live, and then they join the dead.
Anyone who's still among the living has hope. A live dog is better off than a dead lion.
The living know they're going to die. The dead know nothing and have no more reward coming. People have forgotten them.
Their love, their hate, and their envy died out long ago. They'll never again have a share in anything done under the sun.
Go on. Eat your bread with joy and drink your wine with a glad heart. God has already accepted what you've done.
Keep your clothes white, and don't let your head go without oil.
Enjoy life with the wife you love through all the fleeting days God gives you under the sun. Those days slip away, and this is your share in life and in all the work you do under the sun.
Whatever your hands find to do, put your full strength into it. There's no work, planning, knowledge, or wisdom in the grave where you're headed.

I looked again under the sun. The fastest person doesn't always win the race, and the strongest doesn't always win the battle. Wise people don't always have food, people with understanding don't always get rich, and skilled people don't always get favor. Time and chance happen to them all.
Nobody knows when their time will come. People get caught when bad times hit suddenly, the way fish get caught in a cruel net or birds in a trap.
I also saw wisdom at work under the sun in a way that really impressed me.
There was a little city with just a few people in it. A powerful king came against it, surrounded it, and built huge siegeworks around it.
A poor man in the city was wise, and his wisdom saved the city. Still, nobody remembered that poor man.
I said, “Wisdom is better than strength.” Even so, people looked down on the poor man's wisdom and wouldn't listen to him.
Quiet words from wise people are worth hearing more than the shouts of a ruler among fools.
Wisdom beats weapons of war, but a single sinner can wreck a lot of good.
Dead flies can make a perfumer's oil stink. That's how a little foolishness can outweigh wisdom and honor.
A wise person's heart leans to the right. A fool's heart leans to the left.
A fool can be walking down the road, run out of sense entirely, and show everybody what a fool they are.
If a ruler gets angry at you, stay where you are. A gentle response can put even serious offenses to rest.
I've seen something wrong under the sun, the kind of mistake that comes from the ruler.
Foolishness gets a seat of honor, while rich people are made to sit down low.
I've seen servants riding horses and princes walking on the ground like servants.
Dig a pit and you might fall into it. Break through a wall and a snake might bite you.
Cut stones out and they can hurt you. Split wood and you can get hurt doing that too.
A dull ax takes more muscle if you don't sharpen it. Skill gets the job done.
If the snake bites before you charm it, what good were the charmer's words?
Wise people speak with grace. A fool's own words swallow them up.
Their talk starts off foolish and ends up in harmful madness.
A fool keeps piling on words. Nobody knows what's coming. Who can tell anyone what will happen after they're gone?
Work wears fools out. They don't even know the way into town.
What trouble for a country whose king is a child and whose rulers start feasting in the morning!
Happy is the land whose king comes from nobles and whose rulers eat at the proper time to get their strength up, without getting drunk.
Get lazy and the roof sags. Keep your hands idle and the house starts leaking.
People throw a feast to laugh, wine brings cheer to life, and money pays for it all.
Don't curse the king, even in your head. Don't curse rich people in your bedroom. A bird might carry your words, and something with wings could spread the story.
Send your bread out over the waters. After many days you'll find it again.
Share what you have with seven people, even eight. You don't know what disaster might hit the earth.
When clouds are full of rain, they pour it out on the ground. If a tree falls south or north, wherever it lands is where it'll stay.
Keep watching the wind and you'll never plant. Keep staring at the clouds and you'll never harvest.
You don't know which way the wind goes or how bones grow inside a pregnant woman's womb. In the same way, you don't know how God does everything he does.
Plant your seed in the morning, and keep your hands working in the evening. You don't know which planting will do well. It might be this one or that one, or both might turn out just as good.
Light really is sweet. It feels good just to see the sun. ☀️
If you live many years, enjoy every one of them. Remember that the dark days will be many. Everything that comes slips away like a breath.
Young man, enjoy being young. Let your heart be glad in these days. Go where your heart leads and follow what catches your eye. Just know God will bring you to account for all of it.
So clear sorrow out of your heart and put trouble away from your body. Youth and the first light of life slip away like a breath.
Remember your Creator while you're young, before the hard days come and the years get here when you'll say, “I don't enjoy these days at all.”
Remember before the sun and its light go dark, before the moon and stars dim, and before the clouds come back after the rain.
That's the day the keepers of the house will shake and the strong men will bend over. The grinders will stop because there are so few, and the people looking out the windows will lose their light.
The doors to the street will shut. The sound of grinding will grow faint. A bird's call will be enough to wake you, and every voice of music will grow quiet.

Heights will scare you, and the road will be full of fears. The almond tree will bloom, even a grasshopper will be a burden, and desire will fade. People are heading to their home that lasts forever, and mourners walk the streets.
Remember before the silver cord snaps or the gold bowl shatters, before the pitcher breaks at the spring or the wheel breaks at the cistern.
Then the dust goes back to the earth it came from, and the spirit goes back to God who gave it.
“A breath, just a breath,” says the Preacher. “It all slips away like a breath!”
The Preacher was wise, and he kept teaching people what he knew. He thought things through, searched them out, and put many proverbs in order.
The Preacher looked for words people could take in, and what he wrote was honest and true.
Words from wise people are like sharp sticks that prod you. The words of those who teach the gatherings are like nails hammered in tight. They come from one shepherd.
One more thing, my son. Take this warning. There's no end to making books, and too much studying wears your body out.
Here's where it all lands now that you've heard everything. Stand in awe of God and keep his commands. That's the whole duty of a human being.
God will judge everything people do, including everything done in secret, whether it's good or evil.
